source_text: πλῆθος τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ πρὸς ἑσπέραν.» Ὥρα γὰρ ἡ δεκάτη λέγεται καθ' ἣν ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν ὁ Ἐμμανουὴλ, πρὸς αὐτῇ λοιπὸν τῇ ἑσπέρᾳ, τοῦτ' ἔστι τῷ τέλει τοῦ ἐνεστῶτος καιροῦ. Θνησιμαῖον δὲ καὶ θηριάλωτον, οὐ μεῖον ἢ λέπρα τοῖς ἐφαπτομένοις τὸν μολυσμὸν ἐνίησι νοητῶς· τοῦ μὲν θνησιμαίου τὸ τελείως νεκρὸν καὶ ἀπεψυγμένον, ὡς ἐν ἔργοις τοῖς κατὰ τὴν σάρκα, τοῦ δὲ θηριαλώτου, τὴν ὑπὸ τῷ διαβόλῳ πεσοῦσαν ψυχὴν ἀναφανδὸν σημαίνοντος. Χρῆμα δὲ ὅτι σωτήριον ἀποφοιτᾷν ἀνδρὸς, νεκρὰ φρονεῖν ἐγνωκότος καὶ ἀπεψυγμένου τὸν νοῦν, καὶ τρέφοντος ὥσπερ ἐφ' ἑαυτῷ τὸν Σατανᾶν (κατεσθίει γὰρ ἃς ἂν ἕλοιτο ψυχὰς), πῶς οὐκ ἂν εἴη σαφὲς τοῖς γε ἀληθῶς ἀρτίφροσι, καὶ ἀπωτάτω χωρεῖν παντὸς τοῦ καταμολύνειν εἰωθότος ἄριστα διεσπουδακόσιν; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὧδε ἔχει. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἐπειδὴ δὲ πρὸς τοῦτο λοιπὸν ἀκριβείας ἡμῖν ἐξέρπει τὰ διηγήματα, καὶ ὁ τοῦ νόμου σκοπὸς ἥκιστα μὲν τοῖς μεμολυσμένοις ἂν εἴη γε μὴν τοῖς ἀμωμήτως ἔχουσι τὸ χρῆναι μεταλαχεῖν τῶν ἁγίων καὶ ζωοποιῶν ἐδεσμάτων· διίστησιν εὐθὺς εὖ μάλα τὰ γένη, καὶ τίνες ἂν εἶεν οἱ τῆς εὐλογίας ἄξιοι, καὶ πρός γε τοῦτο διᾴττειν οἷοί τε, ὥρισται· τίσι δὲ αὖ τὸ ἀποσοβεῖσθαι πρέπει τῶν ἱερῶν ἐδωδίμων, διεσάφει λέγων· «Καὶ πᾶς ἀλλογενὴς οὐ φάγεται ἅγια· πάροικος ἱερέως ἢ μισθωτὸς, οὐ φάγεται ἅγια. Ἐὰν δὲ ἱερεὺς κτήσηται ψυχὴν ἔκκτητον ἀργυρίου, οὗτος φάγεται τὸν ἄρτον αὐτοῦ, καὶ οἱ οἰκογενεῖς αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὗτοι φάγονται τῶν ἄρτων αὐτοῦ.» Ἐξείργει μὲν ὡς μεμολυσμένον καὶ ἀναπόνιπτον ἔτι τὸν ἀλλογενῆ τε καὶ ἔκφυλον, τοῦτ' ἔστι τὸν οὔπω πεπιστευκότα καὶ Θεὸν οὐκ εἰδότα τὸν ἀληθινόν. Οἷς γὰρ οὐκ ἔνεστι τὸ διὰ τῆς ἐν πνεύματι καὶ νοητῆς οἰκειότητος συνδεῖσθαι Χριστῷ τῷ μεγάλῳ καὶ ἀληθῶς ἱερεῖ, πῶς ἂν οἱ τοιοίδε γένοιντο μέτοχοι τῶν ἄρτων αὐτοῦ; Δώσομεν γὰρ οὐχὶ τὰ ἅγια τοῖς κυσὶ, παραῤῥίψειε δ' ἂν οὐδεὶς τοὺς νοητοὺς μαργαρίτας ἔμπροσθεν τῶν χοίρων, κατὰ τὴν αὐτοῦ τοῦ Σωτῆρος φωνήν. Οὐκοῦν ἀμέτοχος μὲν ὁλοτρόπως ὁ ἀλλογενής. Συνάπτει δὲ τούτῳ τὸν πάροικόν τε καὶ μισθωτόν· εἶεν δ' ἂν οὗτοι πάλιν, κατά γε τὸ αὐτῷ μοι δοκοῦν, οἱ κόσμῳ μὲν ζῶντες, καὶ αὐτῷ πολιτευόμενοι, καὶ οἱονεὶ πατρίδα πεποιημένοι τὴν γῆν, διά γε τοῦ μόνα φρονεῖν τὰ σαρκὸς, ἐν ψιλῇ δὲ ὥσπερ καὶ μόνῃ παροικοῦντες τῇ πίστει, τὴν εἰς Χριστὸν ἀγάπησιν. Καὶ ὅσον μὲν ἧκεν εἰς λόγους, χρηστοὶ καὶ ἐπιεικεῖς· τὸ δ' οὖν εἰς ἔργα καὶ τρόπους τῆς ἀληθοῦς εὐλαβείας, πολὺ δὴ λίαν ἐξεστηκότες. Μισθωτοὶ δὲ αὖ, καὶ αὐτό που τάχα τὸ πιστεῦσαι μόνον, οὐκ αἰδοῖ τῇ πρὸς ἀλήθειαν ᾑρημένοι, μισθὸν δὲ ὥσπερ τινὰ τοῦ δοκεῖν εἶναι Χριστιανοὶ, τὸ ἀρέσκειν τισὶ θηρώμενοι, καὶ τὰς ἐκ τῶν ὠφελεῖν δυναμένων αὐτοὺς φροντίδας θωπευτικῶς ὑποτρέχοντες, καὶ πορισμὸν ποιούμενοι τὴν εὐσέβειαν καὶ φιλοκερδείας προκάλυμμα, τὸ χρηστοεπὲς καθάπερ προσωπεῖον ἑαυτοῖς περιπλάττοντες. Ὅσον μὲν οὖν ἧκεν εἰς νόμου δύναμιν,
pass_a_gloss: [all the] multitude of the sons of Israel toward evening.' For the tenth hour is said to be the one at which Emmanuel appeared to us, near the evening itself now, that is, the end of the present time. And what died of itself and what was caught by beasts sends into those touching a defilement no less than leprosy, spiritually: the thing dead of itself signifying the wholly dead and chilled, as in the works according to the flesh, and the thing caught by beasts openly signifying the soul fallen under the devil. That it is a saving matter to go away from a man who has resolved to think dead things and is chilled in mind, and who feeds Satan as it were on himself (for he devours the souls he may choose), how would it not be clear to those truly sound-minded, and who have been most zealous to go very far from everything accustomed to defile? PALL.: So it is. CYR.: And since our accounts now creep out to this point of exactness, and the aim of the law would be that sharing in the holy and life-making foods must belong least to the defiled, but to those who are blameless, he at once distinguishes very well the kinds, and it is defined who would be worthy of the blessing and able to dart toward it; and to whom again it is fitting to be driven off from the sacred eatables, he made clear, saying: 'And every foreigner shall not eat holy things; a sojourner of a priest or a hired man shall not eat holy things. But if a priest acquires a soul bought with silver, this one shall eat of his bread, and those born in his house, these too shall eat of his loaves.' He shuts out, as defiled and still unwashed, the foreigner and alien, that is, the one who has not yet believed and does not know the true God. For to whom it is not present to be bound to Christ the great and truly priest through the kinship in spirit and of the mind, how would such become sharers of his loaves? For we shall not give the holy things to the dogs, and no one would throw the spiritual pearls before the swine, according to the voice of the Saviour himself. So the foreigner is wholly without share. And he joins to him the sojourner and hired man; and these again would be, at least as it seems to me, those living to the world and conducting their life by it, and as it were having made the earth their homeland, through thinking only the things of the flesh, and sojourning as it were in a bare and lone faith, the love toward Christ. And as far as came to words, kindly and fair; but as to deeds and ways of true piety, very greatly departed. And hired men again, who chose perhaps even believing itself, not out of reverence for the truth, but hunting, as a kind of wage for seeming to be Christians, to please certain people, and flatteringly running under the cares of those able to benefit them, and making piety a means of gain and a cover of love of gain, molding on themselves fair speech like a mask. As far then as came to the force of the law,
pass_b_english: Cyril: …assembly of the sons of Israel shall slaughter it toward evening’ (Exodus 12:6). For the hour at which Emmanuel appeared to us is said to be the tenth, close now to evening itself, that is, to the end of the present age. What has died of itself and what has been torn by beasts bring defilement, in the spiritual sense, on those who touch them no less than leprosy does. For what has died of itself plainly signifies what is wholly dead and gone cold, as in the works that belong to the flesh, and what is torn by beasts signifies the soul that has fallen under the devil. And it is a saving thing to keep away from a man who has set his mind on dead things and gone cold in his thinking, and who, as it were, makes himself food for Satan, for Satan devours whatever souls he chooses (1 Peter 5:8). How could this fail to be clear to those who are truly sound of mind and have earnestly striven to keep as far as possible from everything that usually defiles?

Cyril: Since our account has now come to this point of precision, and the aim of the law is that the right to share in the holy and life-giving foods should belong not at all to the defiled, but to those who are blameless, he at once draws a careful line between the classes. He has defined who would be worthy of the blessing and able to press on toward it, and he makes clear who ought to be driven away from the sacred food, saying: ‘And no foreigner shall eat holy things; a sojourner with a priest or a hired servant shall not eat holy things. But if a priest acquires a person bought with silver, he shall eat of his bread, and those born in his house, they too shall eat of his bread’ (Leviticus 22:10–11). He shuts out the foreigner, the man of another race, as defiled and still unwashed, that is, the one who has not yet believed and does not know the true God. For how could those who cannot be bound through a spiritual and inward kinship to Christ, the great and true Priest, share in his bread? For we will not give what is holy to the dogs, and no one would throw the spiritual pearls before swine, according to the Savior’s own words (Matthew 7:6). So the foreigner has no share at all. With him he joins the sojourner and the hired servant. These again, in my own view, would be those who live for the world and conduct their lives by it, and have made the earth their homeland, as it were, by minding only the things of the flesh; but in their love for Christ they are only sojourners, living, as it were, in bare faith alone. As far as words go, they are good and reasonable, but in the deeds and ways of true piety they have strayed very far indeed. The hired servants, in turn, would perhaps be those who chose even the bare act of believing not out of reverence for the truth, but hunting for the favor of certain people as a kind of wage for seeming to be Christians; who fawn to win the attentions of those able to benefit them; who make godliness a means of gain (1 Timothy 6:5) and a cover for love of profit, and put on fair words like a mask. As far, then, as the force of the law goes…

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 12 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-quotation: §10 ends πᾶν τὸ, §11 begins πλῆθος τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ πρὸς ἑσπέραν, so the turn starts '…assembly of the sons of Israel shall slaughter it toward evening’'. The quotation is Exodus 12:3 (take a sheep by households) and 12:6 (kept until the fourteenth; the whole assembly slaughters it toward evening), abridged; LXX has πλῆθος συναγωγῆς, which the English renders 'assembly'. 'The tenth is said to be the hour': Cyril turns the tenth day of Exodus 12:3 into a late hour of the world's day; no Gospel text is quoted, so no citation. 'Satan devours whatever souls he chooses' is a clear allusion to 1 Peter 5:8, cited. Leviticus 22:10–11 LXX (ἔγκτητον ἀργυρίου; Migne prints ἔκκτητον). 'Minding only the things of the flesh' echoes Romans 8:5 and 'living for the world' may echo Colossians 2:20; left uncited as loose wording. 'The great and true Priest' recalls Hebrews 4:14 but is a title, not a quotation; uncited. 'Make godliness a means of gain' is 1 Timothy 6:5 (πορισμὸν εἶναι τὴν εὐσέβειαν), cited. Doubtful syntax: ἐν ψιλῇ δὲ ὥσπερ καὶ μόνῃ παροικοῦντες τῇ πίστει, τὴν εἰς Χριστὸν ἀγάπησιν; the accusative is taken as 'in respect of their love for Christ'. The section ends mid-sentence (ὅσον μὲν οὖν ἧκεν εἰς νόμου δύναμιν), rendered 'As far, then, as the force of the law goes…'; the sentence finishes in §12. Review: the opening citation narrowed to Exodus 12:6, since Exodus 12:3 is now cited beside its clause in §10.

Drafted Pass A, kept as written (rewritten as a literal English gloss from the Greek in pass_a_gloss): [πᾶν τὸ] πλῆθος τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ πρὸς ἑσπέραν (end of the Exodus quotation). Ὥρα ἡ δεκάτη is said (λέγεται) at which ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν ὁ Ἐμμανουήλ, πρὸς αὐτῇ τῇ ἑσπέρᾳ = τῷ τέλει τοῦ ἐνεστῶτος καιροῦ. Θνησιμαῖον and θηριάλωτον ἐνίησι (inject) μολυσμόν νοητῶς into those touching, οὐ μεῖον ἢ λέπρα: θνησιμαῖον = τὸ τελείως νεκρὸν καὶ ἀπεψυγμένον (cooled), as in ἔργα κατὰ τὴν σάρκα; θηριάλωτον = the ψυχή fallen ὑπὸ τῷ διαβόλῳ, ἀναφανδὸν σημαίνοντος. That σωτήριον to ἀποφοιτᾶν (go away from) a man νεκρὰ φρονεῖν ἐγνωκότος, ἀπεψυγμένου τὸν νοῦν, τρέφοντος ὥσπερ ἐφ' ἑαυτῷ τὸν Σατανᾶν (κατεσθίει γὰρ ἃς ἂν ἕλοιτο ψυχάς): how not σαφές to τοῖς ἀληθῶς ἀρτίφροσι who διεσπουδακόσι to go ἀπωτάτω from all that defiles? PALL: ὧδε ἔχει. CYR: since τὰ διηγήματα ἐξέρπει to this ἀκρίβεια, and ὁ τοῦ νόμου σκοπός: least (ἥκιστα) to the μεμολυσμένοι, but to οἱ ἀμωμήτως ἔχοντες, τὸ χρῆναι μεταλαχεῖν of the holy and ζωοποιὰ ἐδέσματα; διίστησιν εὖ μάλα τὰ γένη; who ἄξιοι τῆς εὐλογίας and able διᾴττειν (dart, press) toward it, ὥρισται; to whom τὸ ἀποσοβεῖσθαι (be shooed off) τῶν ἱερῶν ἐδωδίμων, διεσάφει: πᾶς ἀλλογενὴς οὐ φάγεται ἅγια; πάροικος ἱερέως ἢ μισθωτὸς οὐ φάγεται ἅγια; if ἱερεὺς κτήσηται ψυχὴν ἔγκτητον ἀργυρίου, he shall eat his bread, and οἱ οἰκογενεῖς, they shall eat his bread. Ἐξείργει (excludes) as μεμολυσμένον καὶ ἀναπόνιπτον the ἀλλογενὴς καὶ ἔκφυλος = the one οὔπω πεπιστευκώς, not knowing Θεὸν τὸν ἀληθινόν. Those for whom οὐκ ἔνεστι συνδεῖσθαι through ἡ ἐν πνεύματι καὶ νοητὴ οἰκειότης with Χριστῷ τῷ μεγάλῳ καὶ ἀληθῶς ἱερεῖ: how μέτοχοι τῶν ἄρτων αὐτοῦ? We shall not give τὰ ἅγια τοῖς κυσί, no one παραρρίψειε τοὺς νοητοὺς μαργαρίτας before swine, per τοῦ Σωτῆρος φωνή. So ἀμέτοχος ὁλοτρόπως the alien. Συνάπτει to him πάροικος and μισθωτός: in my view (κατὰ τὸ αὐτῷ μοι δοκοῦν) those κόσμῳ ζῶντες, αὐτῷ πολιτευόμενοι, having made τὴν γῆν πατρίδα, through μόνα φρονεῖν τὰ σαρκός, παροικοῦντες ἐν ψιλῇ καὶ μόνῃ τῇ πίστει τὴν εἰς Χριστὸν ἀγάπησιν. In λόγοι χρηστοὶ καὶ ἐπιεικεῖς; in ἔργα καὶ τρόποι of ἀληθὴς εὐλάβεια, πολὺ λίαν ἐξεστηκότες. Μισθωτοί: those who perhaps chose even τὸ πιστεῦσαι μόνον οὐκ αἰδοῖ τῇ πρὸς ἀλήθειαν, but as a μισθός for τοῦ δοκεῖν εἶναι Χριστιανοί, θηρώμενοι τὸ ἀρέσκειν τισί, θωπευτικῶς ὑποτρέχοντες τὰς φροντίδας of those able to help them, πορισμὸν ποιούμενοι τὴν εὐσέβειαν καὶ φιλοκερδείας προκάλυμμα, περιπλάττοντες τὸ χρηστοεπὲς like a προσωπεῖον. Ὅσον ἧκεν εἰς νόμου δύναμιν (continues in §12).
